text:
maria (support): forwarding customer repro and logs from Acme Retail. customer is hitting sustained 429s and intermittent auth failures during a bursty ingest. they say they moved from free -> trial paid but still on plan tier 0 (free caps). customer claims bursts up to ~600 req/s, normal is ~30 req/s. they want an emergency burst for the weekend (48h) to avoid order backlog. here's the snippet they sent:

Customer pasted:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json

{"model":"gpt-like-xxl","prompt":"...", "messages": [...], "max_tokens":256}
```
Headers they reported:
```
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c
x-rl-remaining: 0
x-rl-reset: 29
x-auth-status: 200
```
Errors in app log: "429 Rate limit exceeded" followed by a handful of "401 Unauthorized" during retries.

can we triage? customer also pasted billing screenshot that shows current plan = Free with API token created 2026-03-10. they attempted to upgrade but invoice failed (card auth error). need help with temporary allowance and a path to convert to paid. cc @dylan (sales) for commercial path :eyes:

jamie (infra): first pass diagnosis: this is classic per-account token quota + rate-limit smoothing kicking in. the x-rl-remaining:0 + reset~29s indicates they exhausted the per-minute request tokens. the intermittent 401s suggest the client's payment update flow rotated the key or they hit an auth edge (card failure -> token deactivated briefly) — that could cause a cascade of retries that consume remaining quota.

quick repro I ran from our side using their request-id shows repeated 429s within a 40s window. logs:
```
[2026-03-15T18:10:23Z] req=req_0a1b2c status=429 route=/v1/generate acct=acct_98765 burst_bucket=0
[2026-03-15T18:10:54Z] req=req_0a1b2c status=401 route=/v1/auth acct=acct_98765 token_status=rotated
```

recommendation:
- immediate: grant a temporary burst_override for 24 hours (config: multiplier=8, cap=800 req/s, id=OVR-1809-ACME) so customer's workers drain backlog. this is reversible quickly if we see abuse.
- near-term: instruct customer to fix payment method; charge success auto-promotes to paid tier which will raise default quotas. sales to assist if they want guaranteed capacity.
- long-term: suggest moving to Dedicated or Reserved if they have sustained >200 req/s on business-critical window.

maria (support): can infra apply a 24h override now? i'll get card owner to attempt card update and will hold off exposing token until it's stable. also need a ticket link for tracking and for finance to follow up.

jamie (infra): I can apply a temporary override but need a partner in finance to allow billing exception logging. steps I will take:
1) create support ticket SB-1809-ACME with audit notes
2) apply burst_override multiplier=8 for 24 hours (OVR-1809-ACME) scoped to acct_98765 and token sk-XXXX
3) add a rate-limit alert: if 95th percentile latency > 700ms for 2m, auto-revoke override and notify #eng-runtime

command I will run (internal only):
```
POST /internal/admin/overrides
Body: {"account_id":"acct_98765","type":"burst","multiplier":8,"duration_hours":24,"reason":"support emergency: Black Friday surge"}
```

ops-bot: audit record created: SB-1809-ACME by maria (support). override request queued (ticket link: https://internal.redwood/support/SB-1809-ACME). :white_check_mark:

maria (support): thanks jamie and ops-bot. @dylan can you reach out to the customer for payment assistance and confirm if they are willing to sign a short-term MRC or PO? sales will also need to know expected sustained RPS to recommend Dedicated.

dylan (sales): on it. chatted with their TPM — they're willing to pay for guaranteed capacity if we can do a trial allowance this weekend. ask: do we have precedent for 48h vs 24h? finance prefers 24h + documented commitment to convert if usage remains high. i'll propose 24h temp burst + 72h extension if card clears and we get verbal commitment. i'll log commercial ticket: COM-1809-ACME.

jamie (infra): applying override now. note: this is not a permanent quota increase — it's a policy-level override that bypasses the per-minute bucket but still enforces global fairness. if they start hogging GPUs we will throttle further down the stack.

ops-bot: override applied: OVR-1809-ACME active (multiplier=8, expires=2026-03-16T18:12:56Z). monitoring hooks enabled. :rocket:

maria (support): relaying to customer. they asked for a sample retry/backoff guidance for their devs. posting snippet to send them:
```
if (resp.status === 429) {
  await sleep(Math.min(1000 * 2 ** retries, 10000)); // exponential backoff upto 10s
  retry();
}
```
also tell them to honor x-rl-reset header before aggressive retry.

dylan (sales): next steps for sales: capture expected ARR, confirm card attempt window (24h), and if they want a guaranteed SLO we propose Reserved capacity quote. i'll update COM-1809-ACME and ask legal to expedite a short-term addendum if needed.

jamie (infra): logging a small caveat: if they continue to rotate tokens or have concurrent clients that don't honor Retry-After, this will eat the override quickly. advise design change: queue locally and fanout at controlled rate.

maria (support): closing loop here — temporary override active, ticket SB-1809-ACME + COM-1809-ACME created, sales engaged. i'll mark the thread resolved once payment clears or if we need to revoke. :eyes:

ops-bot: note added to SB-1809-ACME: "temporary burst applied; monitor for latency/regression; finance notified."
